module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 36

*References:*
* [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems #36](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.36)
* [CKS05] Cohn, H., Kleinberg, R., Szegedy, B., and Umans, C. "Group-theoretic Algorithms for
  Matrix Multiplication" (Problem 4.7)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter
open scoped Pointwise

namespace Green36

/-- The simultaneous double product property [CKS05, 4.1]. -/
def SimultaneousDoubleProduct {ι H : Type*} [AddCommGroup H]
    (A B : ι → Finset H) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  (∀ i, (A i + B i).card = (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
  (∀ i j k, i ≠ k → Disjoint (A i + B j) (A j + B k))

/-- A variant of the simultaneous double product property, as stated in [Gr24, Problem 36]. -/
def Green36Property {ι H : Type*} [AddCommGroup H]
    (A B : ι → Finset H) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  (∀ i, (A i + B i).card = (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
  (∀ i j k, j ≠ k → Disjoint (A i + B i) (A j + B k))

/--
Do the following exist, for arbitrarily large $n$? An abelian group $H$ with $|H| = n^{2+o(1)}$,
together with subsets $A_1, ..., A_n, B_1, ..., B_n$ satisfying $|A_i||B_i| \ge n^{2-o(1)}$ and
$|A_i + B_i| = |A_i||B_i|$, such that the sets $A_i + B_i$ are disjoint from the sets $A_j + B_k$
($j \neq k$)?

NOTE: according to [CKS05, 4.1], the conditions should be $A_i + B_j$ disjoint from $A_j + B_k$ for
$i \neq k$. See `green_36.variants.cks05`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20]
theorem green_36 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
        ∃ (H : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup H) (_ : Finite H) (A B : Fin n → Finset H),
          (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ Nat.card H ∧ Nat.card H ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 + ε) ∧
          (∀ i, (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
          Green36Property A B := by
  sorry

/-- Variant using the exact simultaneous double product property from [CKS05, 4.1]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20]
theorem green_36.variants.cks05 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
        ∃ (H : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup H) (_ : Finite H) (A B : Fin n → Finset H),
          (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ Nat.card H ∧ Nat.card H ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 + ε) ∧
          (∀ i, (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
          SimultaneousDoubleProduct A B := by
  sorry

-- TODO(jeangud) Add variants mentioned in [Gr24, Problem 36] comments.

end Green36

reformulations.difference: CKS05 Definition 4.1 uses right quotients and the implication a_i(a'_j)⁻¹b_j(b'_k)⁻¹ = 1 ⇒ i = k. Lean specializes to abelian groups and expresses the conditions using sumset cardinality and disjointness.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In additive notation, the double product property is equivalent to injectivity of (a,b) ↦ a+b on A_i × B_i, hence to |A_i+B_i| = |A_i||B_i| for finite sets. The second source condition becomes a_i+b_j = a'_j+b'_k ⇒ i=k, exactly the stated disjointness when i≠k. Proved this equivalence in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean as Review36.sdpp_iff_source.

reformulations.difference: The CKS05 variant uses cross-index disjointness, whereas Green's Problem 36 uses diagonal-versus-off-diagonal disjointness. These predicates differ for fixed families, but the existence questions are equivalent.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Replacing every A_i by −A_i converts Green36Property A B into SimultaneousDoubleProduct (fun i => −A i) B. The CKS equation then becomes a'_j+b_j = a_i+b'_k, precisely an intersection between a diagonal and an off-diagonal sumset. Negation preserves all cardinalities, preserves the double product property, and is involutive. Both the predicate equivalence and the equivalence of the full quantified right-hand sides were proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source's n^{2+o(1)} and n^{2−o(1)} conditions for arbitrarily large n are expressed through bounds with every positive ε and Filter.Frequently atTop. The CKS05 variant uses the same encoding.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Frequently atTop on ℕ means arbitrarily large n. From the Lean formulation, choose witnesses with ε=1/m and successively increasing n; their exponent errors tend to zero. Conversely, a source family with errors tending to zero supplies arbitrarily large witnesses for every fixed ε>0. Using one ε for all bounds is harmless by taking the maximum of the errors. The explicit lower bound on |H| also follows from the lower bound on |A_i||B_i| and |A_i+B_i|=|A_i||B_i| once n>0.

sources_consulted: Ben Green, 100 Open Problems, Problem 36 and its comments, p. 19 (current PDF dated 30 January 2026): https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.36

Cohn, Kleinberg, Szegedy and Umans, Group-theoretic Algorithms for Matrix Multiplication, §2 background definitions and §4, especially Definition 4.1 and Conjecture 4.7. Read the LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0511460
arXiv abstract and version record for CKS05: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0511460
review.notes: Checked both definitions and both theorem statements against the sources. No mathematical defects or status discrepancies found. Lean boundary checks verified that n=0 cannot satisfy the group upper bound, positive n excludes empty A_i or B_i, and the valid n=1 example cannot satisfy the arbitrarily-large requirement by itself. Finite H and AddCommGroup H ensure Nat.card H is a positive finite cardinal. Scratch checks are in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, boundaries.lean and cardinality.lean; the equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependency. The reviewed file was not modified.
